findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (including a guest just added by another guest) can add an unbounded number of arbitrary emails to a booking, turning the endpoint into an email-spam relay with no guest cap or rate limit.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — No check on booking.status or endTime, so guests (and confirmation-style ICS emails) can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-past bookings.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:101 — Seated events get raw Attendee rows created without BookingSeat records or a seatsPerTimeSlot check, bypassing seat limits and corrupting seat accounting.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Blacklist is lowercased but the incoming guest email is not, so `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Attendees are committed to the DB before the calendar update and emails, and the email failure is swallowed with console.log, so the UI reports success while calendar/notifications may not have happened and a retry is rejected as duplicate.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager is built from the caller's credentials, not the organizer's, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests the organizer's calendar references cannot be matched and the calendar update silently no-ops (result is never inspected).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Deduplication is exact-match only and does not dedupe within the request itself, so case variants (`a@x.com`/`A@x.com`) and repeated entries in `guests` create duplicate attendee rows (client-side uniqueness check is trivially bypassed).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Nothing prevents adding the organizer's own email (or the caller's own email) as an attendee, producing a booking where the host is also a guest.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Read-check-then-createMany with no transaction or unique constraint means two concurrent requests with the same email both pass the uniqueness check and insert duplicate attendees.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` requires both, so team ADMINs are silently denied while `teamId ?? 0` is passed for non-team bookings; permission semantics do not match the intent.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — newGuests` is the raw `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee that was resubmitted receives a fresh "scheduled" email instead of the add-guests notice, and blacklisted/filtered emails are silently dropped while the caller sees success.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner requires the user to be both admin and owner, so team ADMINs (non-owners) are wrongly denied; should be `||`.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not, so mixed-case emails (e.g. Foo@Blocked.com) bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS; existing-attendee check is also case-sensitive so duplicate attendees can be created.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Server schema does not enforce uniqueness within `guests`, so a request with repeated emails inserts duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:89 — Attendees are persisted before updateCalendarAttendees runs and that call is not wrapped in try/catch, so a calendar failure throws to the client after a partial (non-transactional) DB update with no rollback.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:156 — EventManager is built with the calling user's credentials, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (wrong user's credentials/destination calendar).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — No check on booking.status/endTime, so guests can be added (and confirmation emails sent) for cancelled, rejected or past bookings.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:166 — sendAddGuestsEmails is passed raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, so a pre-existing attendee listed in input receives the "scheduled" email instead of the "guests added" email.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42 — message` is always a non-empty string (template literal), so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never fires and users see "undefined: ..." when err.data is missing.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:123 — CalendarEvent construction (organizer/attendees/destinationCalendar/videoCallData) is copy-pasted from editLocation.handler.ts instead of being extracted into a shared booking-to-CalendarEvent helper.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:38 — user.credentials: true` is included in the booking query but never used (credentials are fetched again via getUsersCredentials), needlessly loading sensitive credential rows.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Variable named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` (admin AND owner), so the name contradicts the logic.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70 — BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env var is parsed inline in the handler rather than via a shared constant/config, and the guest emails are not lowercased before comparison so the lowercase map is inconsistent.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:81 — Reusing the client validation key `emails_must_be_unique_valid` for the "all guests already attendees or blacklisted" case produces a misleading error message.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:126 — booking.eventType?.title as string` cast is unnecessary since title is already typed as string.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — Email send failure is swallowed with a bare console.log that drops the error object; use the logger and include err.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:173 — Hardcoded English `{ message: "Guests added" }` return value is not translated and is unused by the client.
packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:46 — Tooltip content "Remove email" is a hardcoded untranslated string despite `t` being available.
packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:64 — The "add another empty email" logic is duplicated in two Button onClick handlers; extract a single addEmail callback.
packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:14 — Reassigning the `value` prop (`value = value || []`) mutates function parameters; use a default in destructuring instead.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — Zod schema is recreated inside the component on every render and duplicates/diverges from addGuests.schema.ts (server schema lacks the uniqueness refine).
apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:44 — message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` is dead fallback since the template literal is always truthy.
apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:194 — Action id and test id `add_members` are misleading for an add-guests feature; use `add_guests`.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited with no try/catch after the attendees were already persisted, so a calendar/video provider error fails the request with the DB already mutated (client shows error, no emails sent, calendar out of sync, retry hits "emails_must_be_unique_valid").

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:103 — Attendee insert, calendar update, and email send are three non-atomic steps with no transaction or compensation; a failure at any later step leaves guests added in DB but never notified/synced.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Email failure is swallowed with `console.log` and the error object is discarded; use `logger.error` and include `err` so failures are observable.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:548 — Promise.all` over per-recipient sends rejects on the first failure, aborting nothing already in flight but discarding outcomes of the other emails and giving the caller no indication which recipients failed; use `Promise.allSettled` and log per-recipient failures.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:526 — sendAddGuestsEmails` emails every existing attendee and all team members on every add, but the handler passes `guests` (unfiltered input) rather than `uniqueGuests`; pre-existing attendees re-submitted get an AttendeeScheduledEmail duplicate "new booking" instead of the guests-added notice.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:38 — utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` is not awaited/caught inside `onSuccess`, so a refetch rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Blacklist and duplicate filtering compare case-sensitively (`guest === attendee.email`, `includes(guest)` against lowercased list), so mixed-case input bypasses both checks and creates duplicate attendee rows.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — No timeout around external calendar/video API calls in `updateCalendarAttendees`; a hung provider holds the tRPC request open indefinitely after the DB write.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests` array has no max length and is not deduplicated server-side, so any authed user can trigger unbounded attendee inserts and unsolicited emails (sent under the organizer's name with .ics attachments) to arbitrary addresses.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming `guest` is not, so the blacklist is bypassed with mixed-case emails (e.g. Foo@Bar.com).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` should be `||`; as written team admins are denied and the check is effectively owner-only, diverging from the permission model used by sibling handlers (editLocation).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Existing-attendee dedup uses case-sensitive `===`, allowing the same email to be re-added with different casing and re-spammed with invites.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:23 — New addGuests handler (permissions, dedupe, blacklist, calendar update, email fan-out) ships with no unit or integration test at all.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Permission check requires isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner (should be OR) and no permission-matrix test (owner-only admin, attendee, unrelated user, teamId 0 fallback) exists to catch it.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Blacklist and duplicate filtering are case-sensitive (guest not lowercased, attendee email compared with ===) with no tests for mixed-case, partial-duplicate, or all-filtered input paths.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:166 — updateCalendarAttendees is awaited unguarded after DB write, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but no email sent; no test covers this failure ordering or the swallowed sendAddGuestsEmails error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (including a guest just added by another guest) can add an unbounded number of arbitrary emails to a booking, turning the endpoint into an email-spam relay with no guest cap or rate limit.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` endpoint is an `authedProcedure` and explicitly authorizes any existing booking attendee (`isAttendee`) to add guests (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). The input schema allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no max length, and the handler inserts all `uniqueGuests` via `createMany` with no cap. It then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which will generate outbound emails based on the supplied list. This makes it possible for any authenticated attendee to attach an arbitrary number of emails to a booking and trigger email sends, with no guest limit or rate limiting visible in the diff, matching the finding's core concern (spam relay potential).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — No check on booking.status or endTime, so guests (and confirmation-style ICS emails) can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-past bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation fetches the booking and then proceeds to update `booking.attendees`, update the calendar via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and send “guests added” emails/ICS (`sendAddGuestsEmails`) without checking `booking.status` (e.g., CANCELLED/REJECTED/PENDING) or whether `booking.endTime` is in the past. This makes it possible to add guests and send confirmation-style calendar updates for bookings that are cancelled or already over, which is a concrete behavioral/correctness issue visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:101 — Seated events get raw Attendee rows created without BookingSeat records or a seatsPerTimeSlot check, bypassing seat limits and corrupting seat accounting.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally appends new `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without checking any capacity constraint (e.g., `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`) or current attendee count. Since `seatsPerTimeSlot` is explicitly part of the booking’s event type (and is propagated into the `CalendarEvent` later in the handler), this mutation can add attendees beyond the configured seat limit for seated events. The specific assertion about needing `BookingSeat` records is not shown in this diff, but the bypass of seat limits via missing checks is verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Blacklist is lowercased but the incoming guest email is not, so `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same case-sensitivity bug: the blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase, but incoming guest emails are not, allowing bypass with uppercase characters (e.g., Blocked@Example.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Attendees are committed to the DB before the calendar update and emails, and the email failure is swallowed with console.log, so the UI reports success while calendar/notifications may not have happened and a retry is rejected as duplicate.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the code updates the booking attendees in the DB first (prisma.booking.update with createMany) and only afterwards calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the mutation fails but the DB change is already committed, so a retry will typically hit `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and be rejected, leaving calendar state potentially un-updated. Separately, sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped in a try/catch that only console.logs, so the mutation still returns success even if emails fail, meaning the UI can show success while notifications were not sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager is built from the caller's credentials, not the organizer's, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests the organizer's calendar references cannot be matched and the calendar update silently no-ops (result is never inspected).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, after determining permissions, the code fetches the booking (including booking.user.credentials) and separately fetches the organizer user info, but it builds the EventManager using the *caller* (`ctx.user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (lines ~146-159). It then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. For cases where the caller is an attendee or team admin (not the booking organizer), the EventManager will not be initialized with the organizer’s credentials, even though the booking’s calendar references are tied to the organizer’s integrations. This is a concrete mismatch introduced by the diff and can prevent the intended calendar update from occurring for non-organizer callers (regardless of whether the no-op is “silent” internally).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Deduplication is exact-match only and does not dedupe within the request itself, so case variants (`a@x.com`/`A@x.com`) and repeated entries in `guests` create duplicate attendee rows (client-side uniqueness check is trivially bypassed).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Nothing prevents adding the organizer's own email (or the caller's own email) as an attendee, producing a booking where the host is also a guest.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In addGuests.handler.ts the `uniqueGuests` filter (around line ~74) only excludes emails already in `booking.attendees` and those in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. It does not exclude the organizer’s email (`organizer.email` / `booking.userPrimaryEmail`) nor the calling user’s email. Since the organizer is modeled separately from `attendees` (see `evt.organizer` vs `evt.attendees`), it’s possible for the organizer (or caller) to add their own email and have it created as a new attendee via `attendees.createMany`, producing a booking where the host is also an attendee and potentially causing duplicate/confusing emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Read-check-then-createMany with no transaction or unique constraint means two concurrent requests with the same email both pass the uniqueness check and insert duplicate attendees.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler first reads the booking (including attendees), derives `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that in-memory attendee list, then later performs `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` without a transaction and without `skipDuplicates`. This is a classic non-atomic read-check-then-write flow: two concurrent requests can both observe the attendee as absent and both attempt to insert it. Whether the DB ultimately allows duplicates depends on an (unshown) unique constraint, but the diff verifiably introduces the race window and does not enforce uniqueness at the write step.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not, so mixed-case emails (e.g. Foo@Blocked.com) bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS; existing-attendee check is also case-sensitive so duplicate attendees can be created.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is explicitly lowercased (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the check uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing `guest`. That means a mixed-case guest email (e.g., `Foo@Blocked.com`) will not match a lowercased blacklist entry and can bypass the blacklist. Similarly, the duplicate-attendee prevention uses a strict equality check `guest === attendee.email` without case normalization, so if an existing attendee email differs only by case, it will not be detected and a duplicate attendee record could be created. Both behaviors are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Server schema does not enforce uniqueness within `guests`, so a request with repeated emails inserts duplicate attendee rows via createMany.
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: repeated/duplicate emails in the incoming `guests` list are not deduplicated, so `createMany` can insert multiple attendee rows for the same email when the client submits duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:89 — Attendees are persisted before updateCalendarAttendees runs and that call is not wrapped in try/catch, so a calendar failure throws to the client after a partial (non-transactional) DB update with no rollback.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code performs `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` to persist the new attendees, then later calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` without any try/catch or transactional wrapper. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., external calendar API failure), the TRPC mutation will error back to the client after the DB has already been updated, leaving a partial/non-rolled-back state. Only the subsequent `sendAddGuestsEmails` is guarded by try/catch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:156 — EventManager is built with the calling user's credentials, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (wrong user's credentials/destination calendar).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation permits non-organizers to add guests (it allows isAttendee or team admin/owner). However, the calendar update path builds EventManager with the calling user (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`), then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. When the caller is an attendee or team member, those credentials generally do not correspond to the booking organizer’s connected calendar/destination calendar, so the organizer’s calendar event may not be updated (or the wrong calendar/account could be targeted). This mismatch is directly present in the diff and is a correctness defect for the allowed caller set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — No check on booking.status/endTime, so guests can be added (and confirmation emails sent) for cancelled, rejected or past bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler fetches the booking (including startTime/endTime) and proceeds to update attendees, update the calendar event, and send emails/ICS invites without checking any booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or whether the booking has already ended. The email templates used for this flow also generate an ICS payload with status "CONFIRMED", so invoking this mutation on a cancelled/past booking would still send confirmation-style updates. Nothing in the diff prevents the mutation from being called for such bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:166 — sendAddGuestsEmails is passed raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, so a pre-existing attendee listed in input receives the "scheduled" email instead of the "guests added" email.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted ones), and only those `uniqueGuests` are actually added to the booking. However, it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original raw `guests` input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the logic checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide which template to send; so if the input included an email for an existing attendee, that attendee is incorrectly treated as a “new guest” and will receive the scheduled email instead of the “guests added” notification. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid this mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42 — message` is always a non-empty string (template literal), so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never fires and users see "undefined: ..." when err.data is missing.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `message` via a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. A template literal always returns a string, so `message` will be truthy even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (resulting in e.g. `"undefined: ..."`). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` will never use the fallback, and users can indeed see `undefined: ...` when the error code is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:123 — CalendarEvent construction (organizer/attendees/destinationCalendar/videoCallData) is copy-pasted from editLocation.handler.ts instead of being extracted into a shared booking-to-CalendarEvent helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `addGuests.handler.ts` constructing a `CalendarEvent` inline, but the finding claims it is copy-pasted from `editLocation.handler.ts` and should be extracted into a shared helper. That is (1) not a correctness/security/functional defect—it's a maintainability/refactor suggestion—and (2) not verifiable from this diff because `editLocation.handler.ts` contents are not shown, so the “copy-pasted” assertion cannot be confirmed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:38 — user.credentials: true` is included in the booking query but never used (credentials are fetched again via getUsersCredentials), needlessly loading sensitive credential rows.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking query includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`, but the handler never references `booking.user.credentials` anywhere. The only later use of `booking.user` is `booking.user?.destinationCalendar`, and calendar credentials are fetched separately via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. So this eagerly loads credential rows unnecessarily (and they are sensitive) with no functional need in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Variable named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` (admin AND owner), so the name contradicts the logic.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the boolean `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is defined as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. The variable name and the subsequent permission check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`) imply it should allow either role; as written, a team admin who is not also an owner will incorrectly fail the permission gate. This is a verifiable correctness/authorization logic issue introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70 — BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env var is parsed inline in the handler rather than via a shared constant/config, and the guest emails are not lowercased before comparison so the lowercase map is inconsistent.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler builds `blacklistedGuestEmails` by lowercasing the env var entries (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but later checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is taken directly from `input.guests` without lowercasing/normalization. Because email local-parts are commonly treated case-insensitively in practice, this creates a verifiable mismatch: a blacklisted address like `test@example.com` will not be blocked if the user submits `Test@Example.com`. The note about parsing the env var inline is more of a design/style concern, but the inconsistent casing comparison is a real correctness issue present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:81 — Reusing the client validation key `emails_must_be_unique_valid` for the "all guests already attendees or blacklisted" case produces a misleading error message.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` or are in the blacklist. If `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, the handler throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. That translation key (added in common.json) explicitly says “Emails must be unique and valid”, but this branch can be reached even when all provided emails are valid and unique—e.g., they’re simply already attendees or blacklisted—so the surfaced error message is misleading relative to the actual failure condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:126 — booking.eventType?.title as string` cast is unnecessary since title is already typed as string.

adjudication.rationale: The cited code in addGuests.handler.ts sets `type: (booking.eventType?.title as string) || booking?.title || ""`. Whether the `as string` cast is “unnecessary” is not verifiable from this diff because the TypeScript type of `booking.eventType.title` is defined elsewhere (it could be `string | null`, optional, etc.). Even if it were unnecessary, removing it would be a minor type/style cleanup, not a bug, security issue, or clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — Email send failure is swallowed with a bare console.log that drops the error object; use the logger and include err.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in `try/catch`, but the `catch (err)` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not include/log the `err` object or rethrow. This verifiably swallows the failure and drops the actual error details, making debugging/monitoring difficult.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:173 — Hardcoded English `{ message: "Guests added" }` return value is not translated and is unused by the client.

adjudication.rationale: The handler does return a hardcoded string `{ message: "Guests added" }` (visible at the end of `addGuests.handler.ts`). Also, claiming it is "unused by the client" cannot be verified globally from this diff (other clients could call this mutation). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:46 — Tooltip content "Remove email" is a hardcoded untranslated string despite `t` being available.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the component imports `useLocale` and defines `const { t } = useLocale();`, but at the Tooltip (around the mapped EmailField addOnSuffix) it uses a hardcoded string: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">`. This bypasses localization even though translations are intended/available via `t`, so the finding is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:64 — The "add another empty email" logic is duplicated in two Button onClick handlers; extract a single addEmail callback.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, there are indeed two `Button` `onClick` handlers that both do `const updatedValue = [...value]; updatedValue.push(""); setValue(updatedValue);` (the "add another" button and the initial "add emails" button). However, this is purely a refactor/DRY suggestion (code duplication) and not a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:14 — Reassigning the `value` prop (`value = value || []`) mutates function parameters; use a default in destructuring instead.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the line `value = value || [];` only reassigns the local function parameter variable and does not mutate the caller’s prop object/array. Additionally, `value` is typed as a required `string[]` in `MultiEmailProps`, so `value` should not be `undefined` in normal usage, making this line redundant. This is at most a style/lint preference (e.g., avoiding param reassignment), not a clear defect or correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — Zod schema is recreated inside the component on every render and duplicates/diverges from addGuests.schema.ts (server schema lacks the uniqueness refine).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the ZAddGuestsInputSchema is defined inside the React component (so it is recreated on every render) and it adds a uniqueness `.refine(...)`. On the server, addGuests.schema.ts defines ZAddGuestsInputSchema without that uniqueness constraint. This is a real divergence: the server handler also does not dedupe duplicates within the `guests` array (it only filters out existing attendees/blacklisted emails), so a client can bypass the UI and submit duplicate emails, potentially causing duplicate attendee creation attempts (and possible DB constraint errors or inconsistent behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:44 — message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` is dead fallback since the template literal is always truthy.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the onError handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always produces a string, and even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` and/or `t(err.message)` is empty, the result will still be a non-empty string like `"undefined: "` or `": "`, which is truthy. Therefore the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback will never be used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:194 — Action id and test id `add_members` are misleading for an add-guests feature; use `add_guests`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited with no try/catch after the attendees were already persisted, so a calendar/video provider error fails the request with the DB already mutated (client shows error, no emails sent, calendar out of sync, retry hits "emails_must_be_unique_valid").

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the code first persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update(...createMany...) and only afterwards does it `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch or transaction/rollback. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g., calendar provider error), the mutation will reject even though the DB has already been mutated, and the subsequent email-sending block won’t run. A retry will likely compute `uniqueGuests` as empty because the guests are now present in booking.attendees, triggering the BAD_REQUEST (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`). This inconsistency is directly verifiable from the diff’s control flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:103 — Attendee insert, calendar update, and email send are three non-atomic steps with no transaction or compensation; a failure at any later step leaves guests added in DB but never notified/synced.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, guests are first persisted via prisma.booking.update(... createMany ...) and only afterwards the code calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) and then sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests). There is no DB transaction wrapping the write + subsequent side effects, and there is no rollback/compensation if updateCalendarAttendees throws (it’s awaited outside any try/catch) or if email sending fails (it’s caught and only logs, still returning success). This can leave the DB updated while external calendar sync and/or notifications were not performed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Email failure is swallowed with `console.log` and the error object is discarded; use `logger.error` and include `err` so failures are observable.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch`, but the `catch (err)` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log/propagate the actual `err`. This means email-send failures become hard to observe/debug and the error details are discarded, which is a verifiable issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:548 — Promise.all` over per-recipient sends rejects on the first failure, aborting nothing already in flight but discarding outcomes of the other emails and giving the caller no indication which recipients failed; use `Promise.allSettled` and log per-recipient failures.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `sendAddGuestsEmails` which builds an array of `sendEmail(...)` promises and awaits `Promise.all(emailsToSend)`. While it’s true that `Promise.all` rejects on the first rejection and doesn’t provide per-recipient success/failure breakdown, that behavior is not inherently incorrect or a verifiable defect in this diff—it's a design choice commonly used elsewhere (e.g., existing `sendLocationChangeEmails` also uses `Promise.all`). Additionally, the caller (`addGuests.handler.ts`) wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails` in a `try/catch` and intentionally swallows failures, so switching to `allSettled` would be an enhancement for observability, not a clear bug introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:526 — sendAddGuestsEmails` emails every existing attendee and all team members on every add, but the handler passes `guests` (unfiltered input) rather than `uniqueGuests`; pre-existing attendees re-submitted get an AttendeeScheduledEmail duplicate "new booking" instead of the guests-added notice.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted), and only creates new attendee records from `uniqueGuests`. However it then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered `guests` input. In email-manager.ts `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` decides which template to send per attendee using `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) { AttendeeScheduledEmail } else { AttendeeAddGuestsEmail }`. So if the input included an email that was already an attendee (or duplicates), that existing attendee will be treated as a “new guest” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (i.e., the scheduled/new-booking email) instead of the guests-added/update email, even though they were not newly added. This is a concrete logic bug introduced by passing `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` (or the actually-added list).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — Toast message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` which is always truthy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never fires and users see raw strings like "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR: undefined" or untranslated Prisma/calendar error text.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler does `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)`. A template literal always produces a string; even when both parts are `undefined` it becomes something like `"undefined: undefined"`, which is truthy. Therefore the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback will never execute, and users can indeed see raw/unhelpful text such as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR: undefined` or untranslated error strings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:38 — utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` is not awaited/caught inside `onSuccess`, so a refetch rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `onSuccess` is `async` and calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` without `await`. While this means the returned promise is ignored, the finding’s claim that this will cause an unhandled promise rejection due to a refetch failure is not verifiable from the diff. The diff provides no evidence that `invalidate()` can reject in a way that would surface as an unhandled rejection (in many React Query/tRPC setups, invalidation/refetch errors are handled via query state rather than promise rejection). Thus the finding relies on speculative behavior not shown in the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Blacklist and duplicate filtering compare case-sensitively (`guest === attendee.email`, `includes(guest)` against lowercased list), so mixed-case input bypasses both checks and creates duplicate attendee rows.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(...toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` string is compared without normalization (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Likewise, duplicate prevention checks exact string equality against existing attendee emails (`guest === attendee.email`). Since email local-parts are effectively case-insensitive in most systems and the input schema (`z.string().email()`) does not lowercase, a mixed-case input like `Bad@Example.com` can bypass the lowercase blacklist, and `Test@Example.com` can bypass the duplicate check if stored emails are lowercase (or vice versa), resulting in duplicate attendee rows being created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — No timeout around external calendar/video API calls in `updateCalendarAttendees`; a hung provider holds the tRPC request open indefinitely after the DB write.

adjudication.rationale: The new handler does `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` after writing attendees to the DB, but the diff does not show what `updateCalendarAttendees` does internally (whether it calls external providers, and whether it has its own timeout/retry/circuit-breaker logic). Claiming “no timeout around external calendar/video API calls” is not verifiable from this diff alone; it depends on the implementation of `EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, which is outside the shown changes. While the handler itself doesn’t wrap the call in a timeout, that absence is not proof that the overall operation can hang indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests` array has no max length and is not deduplicated server-side, so any authed user can trigger unbounded attendee inserts and unsolicited emails (sent under the organizer's name with .ics attachments) to arbitrary addresses.

adjudication.rationale: The schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (or similar) bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server does not deduplicate input emails: `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` filters out existing attendees/blacklisted emails but will keep duplicates within `guests` itself, and those duplicates are then passed to `attendees.createMany` and also used in `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. Because the API is an authed mutation and accepts arbitrary-length arrays, a permitted caller (organizer or any existing attendee per the permission check) can submit a very large list to trigger large DB inserts and a large number of outbound emails/ICS generation. The finding’s “any authed user” wording is slightly overstated (caller must be organizer/attendee/team admin/owner), but the lack of server-side max length and dedupe, and the potential for abuse/spam, are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming `guest` is not, so the blacklist is bypassed with mixed-case emails (e.g. Foo@Bar.com).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is built as `split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`, but the filter uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing `guest` (or attendee emails) to lowercase. Since email local-parts can be submitted with mixed case, a blacklisted address like `foo@bar.com` can bypass the check by submitting `Foo@Bar.com` (string comparison is case-sensitive). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` should be `||`; as written team admins are denied and the check is effectively owner-only, diverging from the permission model used by sibling handlers (editLocation).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass, which makes the check effectively owner-only (or even stricter) and contradicts the variable name/intent (“AdminOrOwner”). As a result, a legitimate team admin (but not owner) would be denied by the subsequent `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` permission gate. Changing `&&` to `||` would match the stated intent of allowing either role.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Authorization granted solely by matching the session email against unverified, booker-supplied attendee emails (case-sensitive compare, no verified/booking-status check) lets any attendee mutate the organizer's booking, push calendar updates via the organizer's event and mass-email all attendees.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Existing-attendee dedup uses case-sensitive `===`, allowing the same email to be re-added with different casing and re-spammed with invites.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedup/existing-attendee check is `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and the blacklist check is `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Neither normalizes casing (e.g., `toLowerCase()`), so `Test@Example.com` and `test@example.com` are treated as different. That allows re-adding an already-present email with different casing, leading to duplicate attendee rows and repeated calendar/email notifications (spam).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:38 — Booking owner's full `credentials` rows (OAuth tokens/keys) are loaded into memory before the permission check and never used; drop `credentials: true` to avoid needless secret handling.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`. The subsequent permission checks (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isOrganizer`, `isAttendee`) do not use `booking.user.credentials`, and later calendar credentials are fetched via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` instead. So the booking owner's credential rows are unnecessarily loaded into memory even for callers who may fail the permission check, and they are never used afterward; removing `credentials: true` is a verifiable improvement/security hardening.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — NOT_FOUND is returned before the authorization check while FORBIDDEN is returned after, letting any authed user enumerate which booking IDs exist.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code fetches the booking first and immediately throws `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", ... })` if it doesn’t exist, before any permission checks. Only after that it computes `isTeamAdminOrOwner` / `isOrganizer` / `isAttendee` and throws `FORBIDDEN` when unauthorized. This creates an observable difference (`NOT_FOUND` vs `FORBIDDEN`) for arbitrary booking IDs, allowing any authenticated caller of the `authedProcedure` to infer which booking IDs exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:23 — New addGuests handler (permissions, dedupe, blacklist, calendar update, email fan-out) ships with no unit or integration test at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the new `addGuests` handler and related UI/email code, and it does not add any test files. However, the proposed finding claims this “ships with no unit or integration test at all,” which is not a concrete defect introduced by the diff itself and isn’t strictly verifiable from the diff without an explicit project requirement that new handlers must include tests. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Permission check requires isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner (should be OR) and no permission-matrix test (owner-only admin, attendee, unrelated user, teamId 0 fallback) exists to catch it.

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts` the permission flag is computed as:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

Despite the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, the logic requires the user to be **both** a team admin **and** a team owner. That will incorrectly deny access to legitimate users who are only admins or only owners, making the subsequent check:

```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```

stricter than intended. This is a concrete, verifiable correctness/authorization bug introduced by the diff. The note about lacking a permission-matrix test is also consistent with the diff (no tests were added here), though the main actionable defect is the `&&` vs `||` logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Blacklist and duplicate filtering are case-sensitive (guest not lowercased, attendee email compared with ===) with no tests for mixed-case, partial-duplicate, or all-filtered input paths.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase, but the incoming `guests` values are not. The filtering uses exact comparisons (`guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so mixed-case emails can bypass the blacklist and can be added even if the same email already exists with different casing. This is a concrete correctness/security issue introduced by the diff. The “no tests” portion is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone (it only shows no tests were added here), but the case-sensitivity bug itself is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:166 — updateCalendarAttendees is awaited unguarded after DB write, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but no email sent; no test covers this failure ordering or the swallowed sendAddGuestsEmails error.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... createMany ...)` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` without any try/catch or rollback logic. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., external calendar API failure), the mutation will error out before reaching the email-sending block, leaving the DB updated but the calendar/emails not updated—an observable consistency/correctness problem introduced by the ordering. Separately, `sendAddGuestsEmails` errors are explicitly swallowed (`try/catch` with only `console.log`), which can hide failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — sendAddGuestsEmails fan-out (organizer, team members, new guests get scheduled email vs existing attendees get add-guests email) is untested; it is passed raw guests rather than uniqueGuests so filtered emails are misclassified.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees` and any blacklisted emails, and only those are actually inserted (`createMany` uses `guestsFullDetails` built from `uniqueGuests`). However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input `guests` (not `uniqueGuests`). In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`email-manager.ts`), the code classifies each attendee by `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide which template to send. If the raw input contains an existing attendee email (filtered out, so not a “new guest”), that attendee will be misclassified as “new” and receive the wrong email template. The claim about being untested is not verifiable from the diff, but the misclassification due to passing raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` is a real, concrete defect introduced by the diff.
